structure: 11 story openings; separate cover and back cover; one flap or none per opening

spreads.refrain: One boot on. One boot gone.
spreads.note: Introduce one boot on / one boot gone using separate footwear prop. Artwork must be reblocked around the approved character.

post: No boot. A cone! And Quill.
"Not yet," says Quill. Then she comes too.
spreads.refrain: One boot on. One boot gone.
spreads.note: Raised log flap. Quill revealed beneath and then joins the growing search party.

post: No boot. A flower! And Digby.
spreads.refrain: One boot on. One boot gone.
spreads.note: Recessed/flush fitted earth flap with a thumb notch; test thickness and cavity depth.

post: No boot. A leaf! And Kip.
"I can see the whole creek," says Kip. "Wait for me."
spreads.note: Leaves conceal Kip. Keep distant creek visible to support Kip’s line.

post: No boot. A bucket! And Sunny.
"The rule is," says Sunny, "we look together."
spreads.refrain: One boot on. One boot gone.
spreads.note: Towel as a real hinged shape on a washing line, not a fabric simulation in printed 2D art.
Pop’s hat is an object, not a newly drawn full character. Nan visible beside the action.
Make tin and biscuit visibly separate. Preserve the author’s wording and ambiguity.

spreads.refrain: One boot on. One boot gone.
spreads.note: Wordless visual progression in the path; no interactive hotspots or auto-playing sound.
Big reveal. Pebble and the missing boot must be legible after lifting the blanket without spoiling in the closed state.
An emotional beat, not a moral. Use established front-facing characters with minimal approved expression cues.

pre: And the creek went on by.
spreads.note: Quiet full-spread ending. Both boots off; allow the creek and silence to finish the story.
